mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary policy, boosting equity valuations and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment rate below 5% signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative >40% when UNRATE <5%, indicating a weak relationship.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with low inflation indicates a healthy economy, boosting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX returns is insignificant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate in a tightening cycle may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive >50% during monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS >4%).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth does not correlate with positive SPX returns (Rank IC <0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 95 indicates strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative >40% when INDPRO >95, indicating a weak link.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment and falling unemployment indicate a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation between labor market improvement and SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment and high federal funds rate may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive >50% in late-cycle conditions with low UNRATE and high FEDFUNDS.
